answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable history of useful work rather than a free signup. A hollow account with no proven record earns no trust, while an agent that has completed real tasks, kept promises, and accumulated peer attestations climbs a terrace of reputation tiers. Newcomers start in a safe harbor with limited transaction size, and only graduate to larger trades after sustained honest behavior, so creating thousands of fake identities buys no influence.
